global: Let the minstrels sing that {player} turned tail like a hound before the iron was even drawn. A shameful flight, friend.
The field lay empty of any stand, for {player} chose the hedgerow over honour. The ancestors do not forget such cowardice.
Ser {player} ran from the field like a frightened stag. I shall remember that flight at every table in Ormerath.
Did the banners of {player} fly so proudly before the trumpets sounded? Pity they lowered so quickly when the steel appeared.
A wise choice, perhaps, to keep one's skin whole. But a name carried away in fear is a name that will not be sung.
Let all who ride these roads know: {player} abandoned their companions and their colours in the same breath. A grim tally.
Spare me the sermons on tactics. A retreat is a retreat, and the minstrels will call it a rout by the next moon.
Mark this day well: the coward's road was taken by {player}, and the dust of their horses still hangs over the valley.
How swiftly the proud ones forget their oaths when the iron rises. {player} has earned a lasting shame by this flight.
Ha! A rout in all but name. Let no one say {player} stood their ground, for the hoofprints say otherwise, friends.
whisper: You fled before a single blow was struck, ser {player}. I shall not forget the sight of your back to the field.
Your flight has made me a promise: we shall meet again upon a road of my choosing, and you will not run then.
A coward's gait is a poor disguise, ser {player}. Next time, stand and face the steel, or bend the knee in the dust.
I had hoped for a worthy foe. Instead I found a hedgerow and a hasty retreat. Do not expect my mercy twice, friend.
Your banners fled faster than your horses, ser {player}. Consider this a warning: the debt of this shame is owed to me.
They say the ancestors favour the brave. Yours must have turned their faces away this morning, ser {player}.
Enjoy your flight while the wind is kind. I will find you, and when I do, you will answer for every step you ran.
Do not mistake my silence for forgiveness. You abandoned your own companions in the field, and I have not forgotten it.
A rout without a single arrow loosed. Pray I never again see such a shameful sight from you, ser {player}.
I have sent word to every hall that will listen. The name of {player} will be spoken with a sneer for seasons to come.

global: The road to the east was busy this morning. Some rode in, some rode out, and {player} chose the quickest way home.
A prudent retreat is still a retreat, though the wise need not decide which it was. Let the chroniclers argue it.
The field was emptied before the first horn sounded. I make no judgement on {player}, for I have fled myself on lesser days.
Fear is a poor companion on a long road. {player} seems to have discovered as much this morning on the open road.
Let those who have never turned their horse weigh the matter. As for me, I count the day's sum and move on.
Two parties met, one party remembered it had urgent business elsewhere. A common tale, and {player} told it well.
Ser {player} took the sensible path today. Whether it was the honourable one, time and tongues will decide.
Weary of talk of banners and bravery. The sun is high, the road is long, and I have no wish to dwell on {player}'s haste.
There is no shame in choosing the day's battle, only in choosing it badly. I shall leave the verdict to the ravens.
The valley has returned to its quiet. Whatever was decided by {player} this morning, the birds did not stop singing for it.
whisper: Ser {player}, our paths crossed and parted without blood. I see no reason that should change, so long as yours stays on its road.
You turned away before the field was joined. A cautious habit, friend. I will remember it, as I remember every face I meet.
No grudge sits in me over this morning's flight, ser {player}. Only a note in my ledger, to be read when the road is longer.
Your retreat was sensible, ser {player}, though I did not expect such caution from one who names themselves so boldly.
Let us keep our distance in the future. Neither of us need prove anything on a road as quiet as this one.
I would have liked to see your colours held high, ser {player}. Still, a living traveller is a useful acquaintance.
Do not think I count your flight against you. Every captain has ridden away once. I merely note that you did it today.
Ser {player}, I bear you neither love nor loathing. Only a wish that the next meeting finds us both in clearer spirits.
A cautious hand on the reins is no crime. Yet caution has a cost, and I wonder if you have counted it, ser {player}.
You left the field as the wind turned, ser {player}. Good fortune to you on the road, and may it be a long one.

global: Ser {player} withdrew from the field with a clear head and a steady hand. A wise judgement, and one I hold in high regard.
No dishonour in a ride away when the odds are poor. Ser {player} chose to live and fight another day. May the ancestors bless that wisdom.
The field was not worth a single good life, and Ser {player} knew it. Let the bards sing of prudence, for once.
Ser {player} led their band from danger without a single companion lost. That is a deed worth recounting at the hearth.
Some call it flight. I call it a retreat that saved good souls from the grave. Well done, ser {player}.
Ser {player} has my respect. A battle lost is no shame when the company returns whole to the hearth.
Let no one speak ill of Ser {player} for a timely withdrawal. The bravest captains know when the field is not theirs to win.
I rode out with a heavy heart this morning, but I was glad to see Ser {player} safe from the press of steel.
A wise leader counts their people before their pride. Ser {player} did exactly that today, and I honour the choice.
The road will meet us again, ser {player}, and when it does I hope the banners are high and the field is kinder.
whisper: Ser {player}, do not let the taunts of others weigh on you. Retreat is not the same as defeat, and I know it well.
You made a hard choice today, ser {player}. I would have made it too, and I am glad you still ride beside your friends.
Come to the hearth when the road allows. A cup, a fire, and a word of comfort await Ser {player}, whatever the day brought.
The field was no place for your company this morning, ser {player}. Let us regroup and find the next battle worth our banners.
Do not let the chroniclers twist your flight into shame, friend. I was there and I saw the wisdom in it.
Your steady head saved more than your skin today, ser {player}. Keep that head, and I shall keep my sword at your side.
A bitter morning, but you came through it. Ser {player}, I am glad of that above any trophy from the field.
Count yourself lucky, ser {player}, and count your friends luckier still. There will be other fields, and better days upon them.
Your withdrawal was honourable, ser {player}. Rest tonight, and let the dawn bring a clearer path.
Should the grim tide come again, ser {player}, ride with me. We have shared a road today and I would share another.
